subject: mathematics
question_text: If Tan⁻¹x + Tan⁻¹y + Tan⁻¹z = π/2, then prove that xy + yz + zx = 1.

verification.note: Source: Baby Bullet-Q, Junior Inter Maths-1A (Sri Publishers, Machilipatnam), book p.74 — SAQ chapter 12 Inverse Trig Functions, answer 79. Printed appearances: TS 17. The only question in the chapter with no numbers at all. Nothing is evaluated — the three inverses are named as angles and the condition is pushed through the tangent addition formula. ⚠ THE MARK SPLIT IS OURS, NOT THE BOOK'S — no [N Marks] tags are printed against this answer. It is not a bare guess: this same chapter DOES print 1+1+1+1 against answer 77 on book p.73, so the shape is the chapter's own, and the weightings here follow it. The book's chapter header carries ★★ and reads '4 Marks'; that star is the CHAPTER's rank, not this question's. ONE PRESENTATION CHOICE, made deliberately: the book draws a small right triangle beside each answer that needs a second ratio (for example sinα = 4/5 giving cosα = 3/5). Those are authored here as the one-line algebraic step instead, with the triangle route named in the margin note — it keeps the nine answers consistent and avoids three near-identical figures where the algebra is a single line. This is a coaching publication, not a TSBIE document, so the split stays unverified until a Telangana IPE teacher confirms it. Paper position: Maths-1A Section B runs Q11-Q17 at 4 marks each, answer any 5 of 7; Q16 is the Inverse Trig Functions slot. NOTE: Inverse Trigonometric Functions is an SAQ-ONLY unit — the paper gives it no Section-A and no Section-C slot, and this book has no Inverse Trig LAQ chapter (LAQ chapters are 1-6) and no VSAQ chapter (VSAQ chapters are 14-19). recall_prompt: Say how you would prove this — name each move in order, and say which formula you reach for and why.

steps.label: Name the three angles
steps.margin_note: First mark. Let each inverse be an angle, so its tangent is the corresponding letter. The condition then becomes a plain statement about three angles.
steps.memory_tip: Let each inverse be an angle, so its tangent is the matching letter. The condition becomes A + B + C = π/2.

recall.must_convey: That the three inverses are named A, B, C with tanA = x, tanB = y, tanC = z, and the condition becomes A + B + C = π/2.
accept: let each inverse be an angle so tan A is x tan B is y tan C is z and A plus B plus C is pi by two
name the three angles and note their tangents
convert the condition into a statement about three angles
moodintini angles ga peru petti, tan values x y z
take the inverses as A B and C

steps.why: The letters x, y, z are tangents in disguise. Naming the angles is what lets the ordinary tangent formulas be used on them.
common_mistakes: Trying to manipulate the inverses directly.
Forgetting to write down what each tangent equals.

steps.label: Rearrange and take tangents
steps.margin_note: Half the marks. Move C across, then take the tangent of both sides. tan(π/2 − C) is cot C, which is 1/tan C — and that is where the z ends up in a denominator.
steps.memory_tip: Move C across FIRST, then take tangents. tan(π/2 − C) = cot C = 1/tan C, which puts z in a denominator.
lines: A + B + C = π/2 ⇒ A + B = π/2 − C

recall.must_convey: That A + B = π/2 − C, tangents are taken of both sides, and tan(π/2 − C) = cot C = 1/tan C.
accept: move C across then take tan of both sides, tan of pi by two minus C is cot C which is one over tan C
rearrange and use the tangent addition formula on the left
the right side becomes cot C or one over tan C
C ni other side ki teesi tan teeskovali, cot C vasthundi
take tangents of both sides after rearranging

steps.why: tan(90° − θ) = cot θ is what turns the right side into a reciprocal — and it is that reciprocal that produces the symmetric answer.
common_mistakes: Taking tangents before rearranging, which leaves three angles inside one tangent.

steps.label: Substitute and rearrange
steps.margin_note: Last mark. Put the letters back in and cross-multiply. The z distributes over (x+y), and moving the xy across gives the symmetric result.
steps.memory_tip: Cross-multiply: z distributes over (x + y), and moving xy across gives the symmetric result.

recall.must_convey: That substituting gives (x+y)/(1−xy) = 1/z, and cross-multiplying and rearranging gives xy + yz + zx = 1.
accept: substitute the letters back and cross multiply to get z x plus y equals one minus x y then rearrange to x y plus y z plus z x equals one
cross multiply and move the x y across
the answer is x y plus y z plus z x equals one
substitute chesi cross multiply cheste xy plus yz plus zx equals one vasthundi
rearrange to get the symmetric result
heard_as: x y plus y z plus z x

steps.why: The result is symmetric in x, y and z even though the working singled out C — which is a good sign the algebra is right, since the original condition treats all three equally.
common_mistakes: Cross-multiplying the wrong way to x + y = z(1 − xy).
Stopping at zx + yz = 1 − xy without collecting.

insider_note: Move one angle across: A + B = π/2 − C, so tan(A + B) = cot C = 1/z. Cross-multiplying and collecting gives the result with no inverse functions left anywhere.
